prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map clearly separates the near vehicle interior—the overhead sun visor (~0.2–0.4 m), left A-pillar (~0.4–0.6 m), lower dashboard (~0.6–0.9 m), right rearview mirror (~0.5–0.7 m), and the camera wearer's raised left hand in frame 5 (~0.4 m, all within arm's reach)—from the exterior road scene viewed through the windshield. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's head turns slightly leftward so the rearview mirror becomes increasingly clipped at the right edge, while in frame 5 the raised hand partially occludes the lower-center windshield and dashboard. Unlike the RGB image where bright glare washes out the windshield, the depth map provides a clean geometric boundary for the interior cabin surfaces and the raised hand's silhouette. However, the map is unreliable for anything outside the windshield, rendering the entire exterior—including the road, right-side wall, and two pedestrians crossing from ~25 m down to ~10 m ahead—as uniform black at maximum depth with no discernible detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map leaves most of the vehicle interior and outdoor scene unsegmented, detecting only isolated regions across frames 1, 3, 4, and 5. In frame 5, it segments the camera wearer's raised foreground hand (~0.4 m away, within arm's reach, thumb clipped at the bottom edge) as 'person' and also detects one of the pedestrians on the crosswalk (~10–12 m ahead, slightly left of center, walking leftward away from a second unsegmented pedestrian ~1.5 m to their right) as a small 'person' mask, which helps pinpoint that distant figure against the bright windshield glare in RGB. Across frames 1 to 5, the vehicle approaches the crosswalk while the two pedestrians walk from right to left with their bodies oriented sideways to the left rather than facing the camera wearer, though the map only captures the left pedestrian in the final frame. The map is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses all objects in frame 2, misses the second pedestrian throughout, misclassifies the rearview mirror (~0.5 m away on the right) as an 'airplane' in frame 1, labels the lower dashboard (~0.7 m away) as 'car' only in frames 3 and 4, and hallucinated a 'bench' mask over the distant outdoor road/wall area (~15 m ahead) in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1 through 4 and detects only the magenta hand skeleton of the camera wearer's raised left hand in the lower-center foreground of frame 5 (~0.4 m away, well within arm's reach). This skeleton shows the palm facing forward away from the camera wearer with four fingers spread upward in front of the windshield and the thumb base partially clipped at the bottom frame boundary. While it makes the exact finger articulation and joint positions of the raised hand clearer than in the backlit RGB image, it provides no spatial information about the cabin layout, the sun visor above, or the dashboard below. The map is unreliable for the broader scene because it completely fails to detect the body poses or facing directions of the two pedestrians crossing the road from ~25 m to ~10 m ahead across all five frames.
